name: Palimpsest — Overwritten Memory Exchange
description: Palimpsest is a peer-to-peer neural memory marketplace where users buy, sell, and layer recorded experiences directly over their own BCI memory architecture — creating composite identities built from fragments of strangers' lives. Founded in 2209 by former Pulse data architect Saoirse Okonkwo-Dąbrowski in a repurposed server cluster beneath the Halsted Interchange, the platform allows users to 'overwrite' thin experiential layers onto their recall — a process called palimping — so that a Tier 2 dock worker might layer the muscle memory of a concert violinist or the emotional texture of a childhood they never had. Memories are graded by authenticity verification scores, with high-fidelity recordings from Tier 4-5 users commanding premium prices in QUANTA, while unverified Shelf memories sell cheap but carry a cult following for their raw, unprocessed emotional density. The platform operates under a contentious legal gray zone since corponations classify layered memories as 'unlicensed identity modification' rather than content consumption.
cultural_impact: Palimpsest has quietly fractured the concept of authentic personal identity in GLMZ's lower tiers, where users who can't afford physical augmentation use palimped memories as a form of aspirational self-construction — critics call it 'poverty cosplay,' while advocates frame it as radical democratization of lived experience. Employers and housing boards have begun flagging palimped memory signatures in BCI scans, creating a new axis of discrimination against heavy users.
key_figures: Saoirse Okonkwo-Dąbrowski — founder, currently in hiding after Meridian Score litigation
Bastian Ferreira-Ito — top-rated memory vendor, known as 'the Archivist,' sells curated Tier 5 experience packages
Chiamaka Solberg — Shelf memory collective organizer who distributes raw community memories at no cost
locations: Halsted Interchange server cluster, Tier 1-2 border zone
The Sump — a ghost market node beneath Milwaukee Spur where memory chips trade physically
Corridor 9 BCI parlors along the Racine Strip, where palimping sessions are offered as a service
story_hooks: A character purchases what appears to be a mundane Tier 3 childhood memory but discovers it contains a suppressed eyewitness account of a corponation atrocity — and the original seller has gone dark
A Shelf memory collective's entire archive of neighborhood history gets scraped and relisted on Palimpsest by a corporate data broker for profit, erasing the community's claim to its own past
A Tier 4 executive discovers their most private memories have been leaking to Palimpsest for months through a compromised BCI firmware update — and someone is already selling them
user_base: Approximately 340,000 active users; primarily Tier 1-2 with a significant underground Tier 3 presence; heavy concentration among young adults aged 18-35 who cannot afford physical augmentation
monetization: Transaction fees on memory sales (8% cut), tiered listing fees for authenticated high-fidelity recordings, and a subscription service called Palimpsest Deep that provides curated memory bundles and palimping session guides
notable_feature: The Overwrite Stack — a visualization tool that lets users see the accumulated layers of foreign memories integrated into their BCI architecture, displayed as a geological cross-section of borrowed lives
